#+title: Run checks on the build station

Keep the SDK and its native providers on the build station. Send an immutable
test-source snapshot and receive small text receipts.

* Run selected files

Use a host whose Nix daemon has an authenticated remote builder configured.
The [[../../nix/artifact-host.nix][artifact host module]] configures the builder, pinned host key and a
daemon-owned SSH key outside the Nix store.

#+begin_src sh
scripts/ci-check --sdk /absolute/retained-sdk-selection \
  --out .local/checks/core \
  test/bl/core_dotimes_test.bl test/bl/core_switch_test.bl
#+end_src

The SDK selection is an actual immutable Nix product. The command captures
Git-visible source files, including current edits, and refuses changes during
capture. Repository-local file links are materialized into the snapshot.
Each request runs in a bounded VM with a real user manager, 6 GiB RAM,
2 CPUs, no swap and a 24 GiB scratch disk. Local development disables Nix
local execution; the configured station supplies the worker.

Select one complete inventory partition with:

#+begin_src sh
scripts/ci-check --sdk /absolute/retained-sdk-selection \
  --out .local/checks/shard-0 --shard 0 --shards 4
#+end_src

Use =--source /path/to/another/checkout= to capture another tree. Every output
directory must be absent so earlier receipts remain inspectable.

* SDK production and reuse

=--sdk= consumes an existing selection. Without it, the check depends on the
ordinary SDK recipe. =--previous= supplies a retained predecessor whose
validated namespace units can be reused. Requests with the same production
inputs use the same Nix SDK dependency.

SDK metadata is read inside the worker. A thin client can evaluate the normal
recipe without first fetching its completed SDK. Persistent runner policy
must retain the qualified predecessor and its unit store across revisions;
ordinary test-source edits can reuse the existing selection directly.

* Read the result

=result.json= records status, selected files, assertion count, frozen-source
identity, SDK descriptor digest, candidate digest and compiler floor digest.
=files.jsonl= contains per-file outcomes; =run.log= contains test diagnostics.

Physical Nix store roots in returned text become stable opaque SHA-256 labels.
Content digests remain intact. The output has =outputChecks.out.allowedReferences = []=;
unexpected store dependencies make Nix refuse publication. SDK links, binary
payloads and oversized text exports are refused.

A failed test produces an inspectable receipt and the client exits nonzero.
The client requires a passing result for its exact request, unchanged inputs,
nonzero assertions and complete identities. With an explicit SDK, its actual
descriptor digest must also match.

* GitHub Actions

Hosted jobs use Blacksmith x64 Linux runners. They pass =--local= explicitly
to run the same bounded worker on that runner. Development commands omit it
and use the configured station. An unavailable station produces an error.

The Nix-aware Actions cache retains the registered SDK closure, validated
namespace units, pinned model assets and immutable engine source hint across
clean checkouts. Consumers require the producer's exact selector and cache;
they do not start a replacement producer after a cache miss. Rolling releases
consume the successful main CI run's candidate and commit identity.

Builder keys remain daemon-owned host files. Hosted Blacksmith jobs need no
station credentials. A future hosted-to-station route needs an authenticated
managed client; selecting a runner label alone does not establish that route.
